subject: Accounting
title: Adjusting Entries
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Adjusting Entries.

hook.text: Rent paid in advance, salaries earned but not yet paid—these need adjusting entries.

buildup.text: Adjusting entries update accounts so statements reflect the true financial position.

discovery.text: They handle accruals (earned but unpaid) and deferrals (paid but not yet earned).

twist.text: Skip adjustments and a company might report income it hasn't earned or miss expenses it owes.

climax.text: These entries enforce the matching and accrual principles before reports go out.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of adjusting entries?
options: To update accounts at period end

details.summary: Adjusting entries are journal entries made at the end of an accounting period to update accounts that wouldn't otherwise reflect the correct balances. They ensure revenue and expenses are recorded in the period they actually occur, not when cash changes hands.
details.whyItMatters: Without adjusting entries, financial statements would misrepresent the company's actual financial position. They're essential for accrual accounting to work properly.
takeaways: Adjusting entries handle accrued revenue, accrued expenses, prepaid expenses, and unearned revenue
They're made at period-end before financial statements are prepared
Every adjusting entry affects one balance sheet account and one income statement account

faq.question: What are the four types of adjusting entries?
faq.answer: The four types are accrued revenue (earned but not yet received), accrued expenses (incurred but not yet paid), prepaid expenses (paid in advance but not yet consumed), and unearned revenue (received in advance but not yet earned).

faq.question: Why are adjusting entries necessary?
faq.answer: They ensure financial statements reflect the true economic activity of the period. Without them, expenses might be recorded in the wrong period, revenue might be missed or overstated, and the balance sheet would show incorrect asset and liability balances.
